header: DOT MOTOR CARRIER COMPLIANCE AUDIT CHECKLIST

blocks.text: DOT MOTOR CARRIER COMPLIANCE AUDIT CHECKLIST

This Compliance Audit Checklist is used by {{company_name}} ("Company") to audit compliance with federal motor carrier safety regulations (FMCSRs), hazardous materials regulations (HMRs), and other applicable requirements. Audit conducted by: {{auditor_name}} on {{audit_date}}.
Audited Entity: {{audited_entity}} — USDOT Number: {{usdot_number}} — MC Number: {{mc_number}} — Operating Authority: {{operating_authority}}.

rows: USDOT number registered and active on SAFER website
MCS-15 (DOT application) on file and current
MCS-90 (insurance certification) on file, current, and applicable coverage levels
BOC-3 (process agents) filed with FMCSA (if applicable)
Business entity documents (Articles of Incorporation, etc.) on file
Operating authority (MC number) active and applicable commodities listed
State permits, IRP plates, and IRP account current
IFTA license and decals current (if applicable)
Annual update filed with FMCSA (within 12 months)
Tax ID/EIN documented and on file
40/60-hour rule / driver team documentation (if using teams)
Company profile on SAFER website accurate and up to date
DQ File established for each driver, per 49 CFR 391.23
Driver's name, address, and contact information documented
CDL (or non-CDL DL) verified — copy on file, current
CDL endorsements verified ((trailer, hazardous, passenger, tank, etc.) as applicable
Medical examiner's certificate on file, current (not expired)
Medical examination report completed and signed by examiner
MVR (driving record) obtained for preceding 3 years (or more if required)
MVR reviewed — no disqualifying violations (per 49 CFR 391.11)
Road test or equivalent completed and documented (within 12 months of employment)
CDLIS (Commercial Driver's License Information System) check completed
Alcohol and drug testing records on file — pre-employment test completed before first driving
Hazmat background check / TSA security threat assessment (if Hazmat driver)
Driver's education / training records on file
DQ file checklist completed and signed
Driver's annual review of driving record (MVR) completed and on file
Driver signed certification of review of safety regulations (annual)
Driver's qualification file retained for duration of employment + 3 years

blocks.text: SECTION 3: DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTING PROGRAM

rows: Written drug and alcohol policy / testing procedures on file and provided to drivers
Designated employer representative (DER) identified and trained
Consortium / third-party administrator (TPA) contract in place (if applicable)
Collectors, laboratories, MROs, and SAPs identified and certified
Pre-employment drug test completed before first safety-sensitive function (negative result)
Random drug testing pool established — at least 50% of drivers tested annually for drugs
Random alcohol testing pool established — at least 10% of drivers tested annually for alcohol
Random selection process is scientifically valid and documented
Reasonable suspicion training completed for supervisors (minimum 60 minutes for alcohol + 60 minutes for drugs)
Post-accident testing procedures and thresholds documented and followed
Return-to-duty and follow-up testing procedures documented and followed
Testing records maintained and kept confidential — separate from DQ file
Federally regulated drivers identified and listed in testing pool
Testing records and documentation complete and up to date

blocks.text: SECTION 4: HOURS OF SERVICE (HOS) AND LOGS / ELD

rows: ELD registered with FMCSA and installed in each CMV (if required)
ELD data transferred to enforcement officers upon request (REMOTE WRITE/REQUIRED)
ELD malfunction procedures documented and followed (8-day replacement window)
ELD exemption documentation on file (if driver has exemption)
HOS limits enforced — 11-hour driving limit, 14-hour on-duty limit, 30-minute break (if applicable)
60/70-hour limit enforced (60 hours in 7 days or 70 hours in 8 days)
34-hour restart (if used) complies with requirements (2 periods of 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., once per 168 hours)
Driver logs (paper or ELD) reviewed for compliance — no falsification, no missing logs
Annual ELD review completed and driver signed certification
Records of duty status (RODS) retained for 6 months (or per ELD transfer requirements)
Company review of driver logs conducted — at least once every 4 months or per company policy
Drug test results not available for review of HOS compliance (but positive tests may indicate safety issue)

blocks.text: SECTION 5: VEHICLE INSPECTION, MAINTENANCE, AND REPAIRS

rows: Annual motor vehicle inspection completed for each CMV — certificate on file (within 12 months)
Annual inspection stickers / decals affixed (if applicable)
Pre-trip inspection performed and documented by driver before each trip (DVIR)
Post-trip inspection performed and documented by driver after each trip (DVIR)
DVIR reviewed and signed by driver — defects noted and certified as repaired or not requiring repair
Defect repair certification completed (by mechanic) if required
Vehicle maintenance records maintained for each CMV — 12 months minimum
Preventive maintenance schedule established and followed
Tire inspection and maintenance documented — tread depth compliance (4/32 front, 2/32 other)
Brake inspection and adjustment documented — no brakes out of adjustment
All lamps, reflectors, and lighting devices in good working order
Horn, mirrors, windshield wipers, and other required safety equipment functional
Cargo securement equipment maintained — chains, binders, straps, etc. in good condition
Fire extinguisher on board and charged (if required)
Spare fuses and other required ancillary equipment on board (if applicable)
Repair shop / maintenance provider records on file (if outsourced)
Vehicle registry, registration, and title records on file and current
vehicle file retained for 12 months (or 6 months after vehicle is removed from service)

blocks.text: SECTION 6: CARGO, BILLING, AND OTHER COMPLIANCE

rows: Cargo securement plan established and followed for each load
Bill of Lading (BOL) or shipping document completed for each shipment (if applicable)
Hazmat shipping papers completed and placarding correct (if applicable)
Driver has hazmat training and certification (if transporting hazardous materials)
IFTA fuel tax returns filed and paid (if applicable)
IRP apportioned plates and account current (if applicable)
UCR (Unified Carrier Registration) filed and paid annually
Driver files — payroll records, time records, and other records maintained (2-year minimum)
DOT compliance training provided to drivers and staff — documented
Company policies and procedures manual updated and provided to drivers
Any outstanding violations, fines, or penalties tracked and resolved

blocks.text: I certify that this audit was conducted in accordance with Company procedures and applicable regulations, and that the findings stated above are true and accurate to the best of my knowledge.
